task.goal: Make a payment-event ingestion pipeline safely retryable and idempotent while reducing duplicate downstream notifications.
task.context: The pipeline consumes at-least-once events from Kafka, writes payment state to PostgreSQL, and publishes email/webhook notifications. A worker crash after the database commit but before the acknowledgment currently causes duplicate notifications. Traffic is 3,000 events per second with occasional partition rebalances. Downstream webhooks can be slow or unavailable. The team cannot pause ingestion for more than one minute.

constraints.text: A valid payment event must not be silently lost during retries, rebalances, or worker restarts.
The same payment event must not create two state transitions.
Existing webhook payload shape and consumer contracts must remain compatible.
Steady-state ingestion throughput must remain at least 90 percent of the current baseline.
The solution must work with PostgreSQL and Kafka already operated by the team.
Operators should be able to replay a bounded time window safely.

success.text: Repeated delivery of the same event produces one and only one payment state transition.
Retries do not produce duplicate webhook or email notifications.
A crash at every commit/ack boundary recovers without loss or duplicate state.
Benchmark throughput remains at least 90 percent of baseline at 3,000 events per second.
A bounded replay can be executed twice without changing final payment state.

candidates.title: Transactional inbox and outbox
candidates.summary: Record event identity and outgoing notifications in PostgreSQL within one transaction.
candidates.mechanism: Add an inbox table keyed by event_id and an outbox table keyed by notification id. Consume an event, insert the inbox row and payment transition, insert pending notifications, commit, then acknowledge Kafka. A separate dispatcher retries outbox delivery with stable idempotency keys.
assumptions: PostgreSQL write capacity can absorb two additional indexed writes
Webhook consumers tolerate an idempotency key or existing payload identity
risks: Outbox growth requires retention and monitoring
validation: Inject crashes before and after commit/ack
Measure outbox dispatch duplicates and throughput

candidates.title: Kafka transactions and read-process-write
candidates.summary: Use Kafka transactional semantics to atomically publish processing results and offsets.
candidates.mechanism: Move notification events to Kafka, process input partitions in read-process-write transactions, commit offsets transactionally, and let downstream notification workers own delivery retries.
assumptions: All required topics and consumers can use Kafka transactions
PostgreSQL state can be reconciled with transactional Kafka output
risks: Database and Kafka commits are still separate
validation: Run broker and worker failure injection

candidates.title: Unique event index with retry-safe writes
candidates.summary: Use a unique database constraint to make payment transitions idempotent.
candidates.mechanism: Add a unique event_id index and perform insert-on-conflict handling for payment transitions. Keep notifications in the current transaction path and suppress duplicate transition work when the insert conflicts.
assumptions: Every event has a stable globally unique event_id
Notification emission can be safely tied to insert success
risks: A crash after notification but before acknowledgment can still duplicate notifications
Changing notification ordering may affect consumers
validation: Crash between state commit and notification send

candidates.title: Distributed lock per payment
candidates.summary: Serialize processing for a payment key with a Redis or PostgreSQL advisory lock.
candidates.mechanism: Acquire a short-lived lock keyed by payment_id before processing, renew while handling the event, and release after acknowledgment. Keep the existing state and notification writes.
assumptions: Lock service remains available and latency is bounded
Payment keys distribute well enough to avoid hot locks
risks: Locks do not make external notification sends idempotent
Lease expiry can create concurrent processors
validation: Measure lock contention and notification duplicates

candidates.title: Dedicated notification deduplication store
candidates.summary: Keep payment writes unchanged and deduplicate outgoing notifications by stable message id.
candidates.mechanism: Generate a deterministic notification_id from event_id and notification type, write it to a durable store before sending, and suppress repeats when the id already exists. Retry pending sends from the store.
assumptions: Notification identity can be derived without changing payload shape
A durable store can be operated independently
risks: State transition itself remains vulnerable to duplicate processing
The new store becomes another operational dependency
validation: Verify payment state and notification counts separately

candidates.title: In-memory consumer dedup cache
candidates.summary: Suppress recent duplicate event IDs in each worker process.
candidates.mechanism: Keep a bounded TTL cache of processed event IDs in memory and skip events seen recently before entering the transaction.
assumptions: Duplicates arrive within the TTL window
Worker restarts are rare enough for memory loss to be acceptable
risks: Restart or rebalance loses the cache
Memory limits and eviction can reintroduce duplicates
It cannot guarantee no-loss or exactly-once state
